gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 16-inch MacBook Pro ships with a 140 W adapter and a separate MagSafe 3 port, so a 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz screen's 65 W pass-through is under half the Mac's fast-charge wattage and is not needed: the charger goes into MagSafe and the screen takes one Thunderbolt port, natively, with no display driver, on M5 Pro (three external displays) and M5 Max (four).
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's Mac roundup and PCWorld's roundup, both opened in full. Macworld gives the Duex Float 2 Pro's '65W pass-through charging', 'USB-C & Mini HDMI' and optional magnets, and says plain M1/M2 Macs drive one monitor, but never mentions DisplayPort Alt Mode, Apple's 140 W figure, MagSafe, or how many displays a 16-inch Pro drives. PCWorld only advises buying USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode and Power Delivery, with nothing Mac-specific. ChatGPT's own answer already warns not to assume pass-through can power a 16-inch Pro, so only the pairing itself is new. RTINGS' article body did not load and TechRadar's page cut off after its first pick, so those two are not fully compared.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. On a 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max, every candidate with a USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode input runs natively on one Thunderbolt port, and 2560x1600 at 120 Hz is inside Apple's stated per-display limit, so compatibility does not separate the 16-inch 16:10 120 Hz screens. For the Duex Float 2 Pro the page should say: 65 W pass-through (Macworld's figure) against Apple's 140 W adapter, so charge the Mac through MagSafe. The maker's own compatibility cells for our pick (fit range, video path, 120 Hz over USB-C, pass-through wattage) could not be read today because mobilepixels.us returned HTTP 429 on every product-page attempt; they need a re-read before publishing.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro or M5 Max): external displays the Mac drives
findings.value: M5 Pro: up to three external displays; M5 Max: up to four, 'over any combination of Thunderbolt and HDMI ports'; three displays up to 6K at 60 Hz or 4K at 144 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, M5 Pro or M5 Max) - Tech Specs (Apple Support)
findings.note: Apple's figures. 2560x1600 at 120 Hz is below the 4K 144 Hz per-display limit, so the Mac side does not cap a 16-inch 2.5K 120 Hz screen. Only the M5 Pro/Max model page was read; earlier 16-inch generations were not.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro or M5 Max): ports and charging
findings.value: Three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports, HDMI port, MagSafe 3 port; 140 W USB-C Power Adapter in the box; 'Fast-charge capable with 140W or higher USB PD power source'
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, M5 Pro or M5 Max) - Tech Specs (Apple Support)
findings.note: MagSafe 3 is separate from the three Thunderbolt ports, so the Mac's own charger and a one-cable USB-C screen do not compete for a port. Arithmetic: 65 W / 140 W = 46% of the adapter Apple ships.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro or M5 Max): built-in display

findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, M5 Pro or M5 Max) - Tech Specs (Apple Support)
findings.note: Apple's figures. The page states no aspect ratio; 3456/2234 = 1.547, slightly taller than 16:10 (1.6).
